description: Manages advertising campaigns, budgets, bidding and performance reporting.
access_note: A Cloud project starts with Test access. Explorer, Basic and Standard have different production limits and approval paths.
blocker: Production access and quotas depend on the Cloud project's approved level.
toolkit: Start with report queries on test accounts. Require explicit advertiser permissions before enabling edits.
unknowns: The OAuth reference still mentions developer tokens. The September 2026 migration guide supersedes that requirement.

sources.note: Google retired the old developer token and moved access levels to Cloud projects.
Test access and production Explorer, Basic and Standard levels differ in review and operation limits.
The test guide distinguishes the user OAuth and service account flows.
The API exposes REST and gRPC interfaces.
Lists reporting, account management, bidding and campaign management.
Google maintains an MCP server for Google Ads.

description: Creates campaigns and reads audience, creative and performance data for Meta ads.
access_note: App roles and business asset permissions determine what can be tested. Serving client ad accounts requires additional permissions and access review.
blocker: Cross-business campaign management requires business permissions and the appropriate app access level.
toolkit: Prototype an insights reader against an authorized ad account before adding campaign writes.
unknowns: A system user is Meta's business automation identity. Confirm the exact permissions and review for each action.
Developer onboarding cost and official MCP availability were not established by these pages.

sources.note: The Marketing API groups Graph API endpoints for campaigns, audiences and insights.
Meta documents user OAuth and system-user tokens used for automated calls.
Ads Management Standard Access expands operation beyond app admins and developers.
Client permission requirements include ads management and business management.

description: Operates advertising campaigns and reports campaign performance on LinkedIn.
access_note: Development access supports limited edits. Multi-account production writes require Standard access after LinkedIn reviews the integration.
blocker: Expanding write access across customer accounts requires LinkedIn's Standard tier approval.
toolkit: Prototype reporting and limited edits in Development, then apply for production write access.
unknowns: Eligibility differs by marketing product and customer role. No official MCP server was established in this review.

sources.note: Development allows edits to five accounts while broader Standard access requires a request.
Campaign management requires OAuth scopes for member and ad-account access and describes campaign resources.
The quickstart walks through an access token and REST requests to advertising resources.

description: Automates agency CRM, lead management and customer communications.
access_note: Starter includes private integrations. Some operations require a higher subscription. Exact API access during a new trial is unverified.
blocker: Subscription tier and the target agency or location determine usable endpoints.
toolkit: Use scoped contact and task tools for one location. Check entitlement before adding agency-level endpoints.
unknowns: Which endpoints are accessible to a new trial before conversion?

sources.note: HighLevel documents private integration tokens and OAuth 2.0 for its API.
The plan comparison distinguishes starter access from more advanced API capabilities.
HighLevel documents its server and its contact, opportunity and task workflows.
OAuth access tokens are scoped to agency or location contexts.
